rules.what_is_seen: The roof outline drawn around the third-storey block is one long east-west bar running far to the west and east of the block and many times longer than it is deep, with the compact third-storey rooms occupying only its middle.

The roof plan shows two parallel east-west bars, the main roof extending far to the west and a second roof strip set back to the north and offset toward the east so the footprint is a stepped elongated shape, and at this level the baths, hall and closets are gathered in a strip on the east and north sides away from the bedrooms.

The stair marked DOWN is enclosed in hatched masonry walls at the centre of the third-storey block on its long axis between the two bedrooms, with the hall passing it to the south; no hearth is drawn at this level.

The third-storey block is plain rectangular with no prow bays and its west, east and south end walls are drawn as full-width groups of casements between small hatched piers onto balconies, while the ends of the main bar below are hidden under the roof outline.

The three roofs drawn in plan around the block (the west roof, the north-east wing roof and the south-east roof end) are hipped, each with diagonal hip lines meeting at a ridge point; pitch, eave depth and fascia are not readable in plan.

The third-storey block is a small rectangle set back near the middle of a much longer roof outline that extends further west than east, with a wing roof offset to the north-east and the master bedroom stepping out to the south-west, so the massing is stepped and asymmetric.

Every exterior bedroom wall is drawn as casements alternating with short hatched piers dimensioned 8 in pier and 3 ft 4 in light on a 4 ft 0 in module, with 4 ft 0 in grid lines dimensioned along the north and south walls and a smaller 2 ft 6 in light between 8 in piers on the north wall.
Walls are shown in plan as diagonally hatched masonry sections with no brick coursing, caps or bands drawn.
No glazing pattern is drawn; casements appear only as openings between piers in plan.
The three balconies and the balconies below are bounded by low parapets drawn as plain double lines, with no copings, planter boxes or urns drawn and no material readable in plan.

The south wall of the master bedroom is a continuous band of lights between short hatched piers running onto a south balcony the full length of the room and stopping at hatched corner piers; door leaves and swings are not distinguished, and the living-dining south wall is not on this sheet.
No entrance, exterior door, steps or path is drawn on this upper-floor plan, which is reached only by the central stair marked DOWN, so the entrance cannot be assessed.

A thick hatched masonry mass with a small rectangular void, possibly a flue, is drawn at the south-west corner of the master bedroom, but it is unlabelled and no chimney cap or slot openings can be read in plan.
No trim, furniture or profile detail is drawn; bathroom fixtures appear only in plain outline.
The top-storey window bands are drawn in plan as openings between hatched piers, so solid infill panels cannot be distinguished from lights.

do_not_list.what_is_seen: No entrance, steps, path, porch or door surround is drawn on this upper-floor plan, so the entrance cannot be assessed.

The plan massing is asymmetric in both directions: the third-storey block sits on a roof that extends much further west than east, the wing roof is offset to the north-east and the master bedroom steps out to the south-west, so no symmetrical whole-building composition is drawn.
No fireplace, mantel, trim or furniture is drawn at this scale.
Walls are drawn as hatched masonry sections in plan with no brick coursing or joints rendered.
Every roof drawn (the west roof, the north-east wing roof and the south-east roof end) is shown with diagonal hip lines converging on a ridge point, and no gable end is drawn.

No hearth opening is drawn on this floor; a hatched masonry mass with a small rectangular void sits against the west exterior wall at the south-west corner of the master bedroom but is unlabelled and shows no fireplace opening.

notes: Sheet is HABS IL-1005 sheet 3 of 10, Third Floor Plan (Carnegie Institute of Technology 1962, second addendum): the set-back top-storey block (two bedrooms, master bedroom, hall, two baths, closets, central stair marked DOWN) with west, east and south balconies, surrounded by the roof plan of the storeys below (hipped roofs labelled ROOF) and two BALCONY BELOW outlines. Walls are diagonally hatched masonry with casements between short piers on a 4 ft module. Elevational rules (coursing, caps, glazing pattern, chimney caps and slots, trim profiles, infill panels) and the entrance cannot be assessed from this plan. An unlabelled hatched mass with a small void at the south-west corner of the master bedroom, on the west exterior wall, may be a flue or stack; no hearth opening is drawn there.
